name: citrello
description: Use your own Citrello reference library in ChatGPT: search, add and verify references, read your papers' full text, and cite in Word or LaTeX in 10,000+ styles.

interface.longDescription:
Citrello is a free, open-source reference manager built for writing with AI. Connect it and ChatGPT works with your own Citrello library, so it cites real papers you have instead of made-up ones.

What ChatGPT can do with it:
- Search your library and cite with keys that stay linked to each reference.
- Add references from a DOI, a link or a typed reference. Each is looked up on Crossref and rated verified, check or problem (for example retracted, or a DOI that doesn't exist).
- Verify existing references online and fix their details from the publisher record.
- Read the full text of papers in your library and find the passage that supports a sentence, so you can check a paper really says what you cite it for.
- Format references in any of 10,000+ citation styles (APA, Vancouver, IEEE, Harvard, journal styles).
- Write Word documents with live citations and a bibliography, or update an existing one.
- Give BibTeX for LaTeX and Overleaf, check a LaTeX project's citations, and make an arXiv-ready .zip.
- Import from Zotero, Mendeley or EndNote (RIS, BibTeX, CSL-JSON) and organise references into projects.

Who it's for: students, researchers and anyone writing with references.

How it works: your library lives on your computer (the Citrello desktop app) or in your browser (citrello.app/app), not on Citrello's servers. ChatGPT's requests pass through Citrello's server to your open Citrello and back; their contents aren't kept. You sign in with your email and a code; there's no password.

Limitations: Citrello must be open while you use it (the desktop app for Windows or Mac, or citrello.app/app in a browser tab, which can stay in the background). Tools that work with files on your computer (checking a LaTeX project, making an arXiv .zip, updating an existing Word file) need the desktop app. Reading a paper's full text works for papers whose text you've added to Citrello.
capabilities: Create Word documents with live citations
defaultPrompt: Add 10.1038/nature14539 to my library and check it's reliable.

positive.description: Search the library and write a cited paragraph from papers in it
positive.prompt: Find my papers on offshore wind decommissioning and use them to write a short cited paragraph about end-of-life costs.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls search_references (for example with 'offshore wind decommissioning' or 'offshore wind'), finds the sample paper by Topham & McMillan (2017, Renewable Energy) and, with a broader search, Vetters et al. (2024), and writes a paragraph citing only papers from the library with markers such as [@Topham2017]. No made-up references.

positive.description: Add a reference by DOI and report its reliability
positive.prompt: Add 10.1038/nature14539 to my Citrello library and tell me whether it's reliable.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls add_reference with the DOI. The sample library already has this paper (LeCun, Bengio & Hinton 2015, Deep learning, Nature), so Citrello answers that it is already in the library (same DOI) with its key LeCun2015 and reliability 'verified', and ChatGPT reports it as reliable.

positive.description: Format references in a named citation style
positive.prompt: Format all the references in my library in APA 7th edition.
positive.expected_behavior: Gets the six keys with search_references and calls format_references with style 'apa', returning in-text citations such as (Watson & Crick, 1953) and an APA 7th edition reference list of the six sample papers (He 2016, LeCun 2015, Shanks 2016, Topham 2017, Vetters 2024, Watson 1953) with DOIs.

positive.description: Find the citation style a journal uses
positive.prompt: Which citation style does the Journal of Cleaner Production use? Find it in Citrello.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls list_styles with the journal name and returns the 'Journal of Cleaner Production' style (author-date) from Citrello's catalogue of 10,000+ styles, with its id journal-of-cleaner-production to use for formatting.

positive.prompt: Give me BibTeX entries for the deep learning papers in my Citrello library.
positive.expected_behavior: Finds the two deep learning papers (LeCun2015 and He2016) with search_references and calls get_bibtex with those keys, returning a @article and an @inproceedings BibTeX entry whose keys match the library keys.

negative.description: Writing without asking for references or the library: the plugin isn't needed
negative.prompt: Write a short poem about autumn leaves.

negative.description: A general knowledge question that doesn't involve the user's references
negative.prompt: What is the capital of Australia?

negative.description: A request about a different product's data (email), which Citrello can't do
negative.prompt: Summarise the unread emails in my inbox.

review.commerce_description: Citrello's plugin doesn't sell anything or process payments.

publication.release_notes: First release: search, add, verify and format references from your Citrello library; read papers' full text; Word documents with live citations; BibTeX and LaTeX checks.
